etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from New Latin bacteria, plural of bactērium, from Ancient Greek βακτήριον (baktḗrion, “little rod”).

definitions.definition: (US) A type, species, or strain of bacterium.

quote.citation: 2002, A.C. Panchdhari, Water Supply and Sanitary Installations‎[1], 2nd edition, →ISBN, page 177:
quote.text: Anaerobic bacteria function in the absence of oxygen, where as aerobic bacteria require sunlight and also oxygen. Both these bacterias are capable of breaking down the organic matter  […]

definitions.definition: (derogatory, slang) Lowlife, slob (could be treated as plural or singular).

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From New Latin bactēria, from Ancient Greek βακτηρίᾱ (baktēríā, “rod, stick”).

definitions.definition: (dated, medicine) An oval bacterium, as distinguished from a spherical coccus or rod-shaped bacillus.
